extracted.intended_audience: general audience; people who want to improve their speaking/public-speaking skills
extracted.subtask_description: Short-form guidance on how to speak so listeners want to listen, focusing on vocal technique and empathetic delivery for everyday and presentation contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make people want to listen
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the common problem of talking but not being listened to; speaking should be designed to attract and retain listener attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as the central goal of the talk: use techniques and practices that transform ordinary speech into something people want to listen to. (Original phrasing: 'Have you ever felt like you're talking, but nobody is listening?')

rubrics_metrics.name: How-to's of powerful speaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachable techniques and principles that constitute 'powerful speaking.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The talk demonstrates actionable how-to items for powerful speaking; this is the overarching category that includes vocal work and empathetic delivery. (Original phrasing: 'the how-to's of powerful speaking')

rubrics_metrics.name: Handy vocal exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific vocal exercises to improve the voice and delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practicing vocal exercises is presented as a concrete method to enhance speaking power; the page mentions these exercises but does not list specifics. (Original phrasing: 'from some handy vocal exercises')

rubrics_metrics.name: Speak with empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt an empathetic stance in delivery so listeners feel understood and engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tips on speaking with empathy are highlighted as a key component of effective speaking; empathy in tone and content helps connect with audiences. (Original phrasing: 'tips on how to speak with empathy')

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic/affective aim: make the world sound more beautiful
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond technical proficiency, speaking can aim to improve the overall quality and pleasantness of public sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The talk frames speaking not only as functional but as contributing to how the world 'sounds' — an aspirational criterion for speaking quality. (Original phrasing: 'A talk that might help the world sound more beautiful.')
